subject: Risk & Compliance
title: The Cost of Trust
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Cost of Trust.

hook.text: The most trusted person in the organization steals the most. Trust is the ultimate access card.

buildup.text: Senior executives commit fewer frauds but the average loss is ten times higher than lower-level employees.

discovery.text: Long-tenured employees commit larger frauds because they know the systems, controls, and where the gaps are.

twist.text: Companies resist investigating trusted employees. By the time they act, losses are catastrophic.

climax.text: Trust is essential for business but it must be balanced with verification. Trust without controls is a vulnerability.

punchline.text: Trust is necessary. Trust without verification is dangerous.

quiz.question: Who typically causes the largest fraud losses?
options: Senior executives with high trust and access
New employees in their first week
